title: Line 118 aborts the post-install summary on any adb stderr output (PowerShell 5.1 + ErrorActionPreference=Stop + 2>$null)
evidence: env.ps1 sets $ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; install-phone.ps1:118 runs `& $Adb -s $serial shell pidof -s $AppId 2>$null` - the only adb call in the file that is NOT routed through the AdbText helper (cmd /c ... 2>&1). In Windows PowerShell 5.1 a native command whose stderr is redirected turns every stderr line into a terminating NativeCommandError under Stop. Demonstrated: `powershell -NoProfile -Command "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; try { & cmd /c 'echo some-stderr-text 1>&2' 2>$null; 'reached' } catch { 'THREW: ' + $_.Exception.GetType().Name }"` prints `THREW: RemoteException - some-stderr-text`. If adb prints anything to stderr at that moment (device dropped off Wi-Fi: `adb: device '...' not found`, `error: device offline`, ...) the script dies after install + launch + the 45 s logcat capture, before it prints the process state and the filtered WebView/crash lines the main session needs (the raw log file itself is already written).
fix: Replace line 118 with the existing helper, e.g. `$pid_ = (AdbText @('-s', $serial, 'shell', 'pidof', '-s', $AppId))` (AdbText merges stderr via cmd and returns text; a non-empty non-numeric answer means 'not running'), or wrap the call in try/catch with -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue. Same pattern check for the other bare `& $Adb` calls (lines 47, 86, 89, 94, 120) - they currently work because their stderr is not redirected, but they would break if someone adds 2>&1.

title: Owner guide names a button that does not exist ('הרשמה' in the tour banner) and over-warns about an 'unknown source' prompt
evidence: Line 76: "לוחצים **הרשמה** בפס העליון ויוצרים חשבון אמיתי". The tour banner (src/components/GuestBanner.tsx:41) renders tr('mobile.guest.createAccount'), which in shared/i18n/messages/he/mobile.ts is 'יצירת חשבון' - there is no 'הרשמה' control in the banner, so a non-programmer following the guide looks for a label that is not on the screen. Minor precision items in the same file: line 74 writes the Skip label with an en dash "דילוג – רק להסתכל" while the button says 'דילוג - רק להסתכל' (mobile.guest.skip); lines 63-64 say Android may show an "אפליקציה ממקור לא מוכר" warning - an `adb install -r` from a paired computer shows no such dialog (at most a silent Play Protect scan); lines 65-66 say the app asks for no permission - true for prompts, but the manifest does declare the normal INTERNET permission (aapt2: uses-permission android.permission.INTERNET), which Play's listing will show as 'full network access'.
fix: Line 76: 'לוחצים **יצירת חשבון** בפס העליון (פס מצב הסיור)'. Line 74: use the hyphen exactly as on the button. Lines 63-64: drop or soften the unknown-source sentence ('ההתקנה נעשית דרך adb מהמחשב ולכן אין חלון אישור בטלפון'). Lines 65-66: 'לא מבקשת שום הרשאה שצריך לאשר (יש רק הרשאת אינטרנט רגילה, לתוסף הדואר העתידי; האפליקציה עצמה לא פונה לאינטרנט)'.

title: JVM network rules are bypassed by wildcard imports (java.net.* / javax.net.*)
evidence: Scratch tree (deleted afterwards) with android/app/src/main/java/x/Leak.java containing `import java.net.*; import javax.net.*; ... Socket s = SocketFactory.getDefault().createSocket("example.org", 443); s.getOutputStream().write(1);` -> `node scripts/check-no-network.mjs --root=<tree>` prints '✅ Network audit passed ... the Android native code opens no connections' and exits 0. The same tree with the fully-qualified form (`import java.net.Socket; new Socket("example.org", 443)`) is caught (2 violations, exit 1), so the JVM_FORBIDDEN rules (lines 44-50) only match fully-qualified names, `new Socket(`-style constructors and a fixed list of HTTP client libraries; `SocketFactory.getDefault().createSocket(...)`, `SSLSocketFactory`, `Socket` via wildcard import and `HttpsURLConnection` obtained through `URL.openConnection()` on a wildcard-imported `URL` are not covered. The gate therefore does not deliver the 'nothing may open network connections' guarantee WP-14 item 9 asks for; it documents intent.
fix: Add rules such as `{ re: /\bimport\s+javax?\.net\.(?:\*|ssl\.\*)\s*;/g, why: 'wildcard import of a network package' }`, `{ re: /\b(?:SSL)?SocketFactory\b|\bcreateSocket\s*\(|\bopenConnection\s*\(|\bSSLContext\b|\bSSLSocket\b/g, why: 'socket factory / connection' }`, and `{ re: /\b(?:Socket|ServerSocket|DatagramSocket|URL)\s+\w+\s*=/g, why: 'network object' }`; keep the WP-12 allow-list idea (per-file exception for the diary-mail plugin). Add the wildcard-import case to mobile/test/network-audit.test.ts.

title: configChanges omits fontScale: a system font-size change recreates the activity and reloads the WebView (unsaved text lost)
evidence: Merged manifest (aapt2 dump xmltree of app-debug.apk): `configChanges(0x0101001f)=0x00003ff4` = orientation|keyboardHidden|keyboard|screenSize|locale|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout|uiMode|navigation|density|layoutDirection; the fontScale bit (0x40000000) is absent (source line 57). Android recreates an activity for every configuration change not listed, and Capacitor's BridgeActivity reloads the page on recreation, so changing 'Font size' in the phone's settings while an entry is being written restarts the WebView - the very effect the manifest comment on lines 46-50 says the list prevents. The WP text only named rotation/keyboard/locale/density, so this is beyond the stated list, but it is the same owner-visible failure (lost text).
fix: Add `fontScale` (and, for completeness, `colorMode`) to android:configChanges; the web UI already follows the browser font scale via rem units, nothing else needs to change. Re-run `npm run android:apk` (verify-apk does not check the bit) and optionally extend verify-apk.ps1 with a check that the configChanges mask includes 0x40000000.
